proposition: In letters 4 and 12 (ca. 816/1413, Isfahan?) Ibn Turka says he must leave the region for a time because of harassment by envious persons (letter 4) and is moving his family to Shiraz (letter 12); he uses both letters to recommend the young learned Sharaf al-Dīn Yaʿqūb as his replacement (letter 4 to Fīrūzshāh, letter 12 to Iskandar's vizier).

mediation.who: Ibn Turka, writing to Amīr Fīrūzshāh (presumed) and Vazīr Ḥāfiẓ Rāzī
mediation.note: Letters to third parties ask or offer favours; the text survives only in copies made after his lifetime (except the marginal letters in MS Majlis 10196).

mediation.who: Melvin-Koushki, summarising, dating and identifying the letter(s)
mediation.note: Addressee of letter 4 is 'almost certainly' Fīrūzshāh per MK
